scope: Native pure-C Windows application using the existing signed VB-CABLE driver; browser HTML/JavaScript client. Physical cross-device listening remains user validation.
platform: Windows 10 x64 build 19045, Realtek physical output

build.runtime: Windows APIs, no Node/Python/.NET runtime dependency

buffer.changes: new stream epoch; all clients clear old audio and rebuffer; URL unchanged

playback.native: one original PCM frame per output frame; discrete silence/drop corrections
playback.browser: AudioBufferSource playbackRate=1; gaps or late packet drops
playback.calibration: discrete output phase correction; never slews sample rate

unit_tests.browser_deterministic_playback: passed: original speed, drift, late packet drop, reset and 5000 ms queue

native_http_websocket_tests.includes: plain URL without cookies for HTML, client JavaScript, status and WebSocket; cross-origin rejection; 404; reconnect; identical packets; fragmented frames; slow clients

physical_output_timing.measurement: WASAPI physical output vs shared packet play deadlines

browser_ui.remote_audio_scheduling_test: deterministic Web Audio mock; physical remote listening not tested

release_inspection: passed: native x64 PE GUI; manifest-only resources; no installer RCDATA, archive, embedded driver files or extra runtime dependencies
limitations: WASAPI loopback timing is not a microphone/acoustic synchronization measurement.
All automated receivers were on the same PC; cross-device/Wi-Fi/mobile-background testing is assigned to the user.
The 60 second soak used a real VB-CABLE silent stream with four actual WebSocket receivers; it is not four physical playback devices.
One capture discontinuity flag was observed on the initial WASAPI packet; host gap count stayed zero in this run.
50 ms is an input limit, not a stable-latency guarantee on every browser or device.
Windows 11 and other PC hardware were not physically tested.

reused_checks_from_1_1_0.reason: Audio capture/render, manual fixed buffering and playback scheduling unchanged; this patch removes URL access tokens and cookies. Those results retain their original test scope.

reused_checks_from_1_1_1.reason: Only native window layout and buffer-field Enter handling changed; HTTP/WebSocket and audio paths unchanged.

reused_checks_from_1_1_2.reason: Native window controls and Enter handling unchanged. Only installation entry and build/package payloads changed.
